extracted.intended_audience: international patent applicants, their agents/patent attorneys, and PCT practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive standards for representation, correspondence, recording changes, and rectification of mistakes during the PCT international phase (including the effect of the IPRP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and access to IPRP and international preliminary examination file
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Preliminary Examining Authority may not, unless requested or authorized by the applicant, give copies to anyone other than the applicant and the International Bureau; once the IPRP (Chapter II) becomes part of the file in an elected Office, the national law of that Office applies as to access by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access limitations apply during the international phase; elected/national Offices' law governs access after the report is part of the national file (see paragraph 11.072 referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining copies of documents cited in the IPRP (Chapter II)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may obtain copies of those documents cited in the international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter II) which were not cited in the international search report by requesting them from the International Preliminary Examining Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for furnishing copies are shown in Annex E; the request must be made to the IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and usefulness of the IPRP in the national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPRP (Chapter II) contains an opinion on novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness) and industrial applicability and provides a strong basis for evaluating likely national patent grant; it is not binding but carries considerable weight with elected Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A favorable IPRP assists prosecution before elected Offices and an elected Office that acted as IPEA will generally proceed rapidly to grant if the IPRP is favorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes for which an agent may be appointed
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may appoint an agent or agents to represent him/her before the receiving Office, the International Bureau, the International Searching Authority, any Authority specified for supplementary search and the International Preliminary Examining Authority (i.e., for the international phase generally) or specifically before any of those Authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents appointed for the international phase are not automatically agents in the national phase; separate national appointments may be needed for national processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to be appointed as an agent
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may be appointed as agent for the international phase generally if that person has the right to practice before the Office with which the international application is filed; where filed with the International Bureau, any person who has the right to practice before the national (or regional) Office of, or acting for, a Contracting State of which the applicant is a resident or national may be appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For representation before a particular Authority (ISA, SISA, IPEA) the person must have the right to practice before the Office or intergovernmental organization acting as that Authority; the right to practice is governed by the national law applied by the Office or organization concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom for each applicant to appoint their own agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant is free to appoint his/her own agent; however, it is ordinarily convenient for co-applicants to appoint the same person as a common agent or a number of common agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinating representation is a matter of convenience and practice, not a requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-agent appointment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agent appointed for the international phase in general may appoint a sub-agent to represent the applicant, unless the original appointment document indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-agents may be appointed generally or for specific Authorities; a sub-agent's appointment is subject to the same qualifications as set out for agents (right to practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may serve as a common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are two or more applicants and they have not appointed a common agent, one of the applicants may be appointed by the others as their common representative; only a person who is a national or resident of a Contracting State and thus entitled to file an international application may be appointed common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The common representative is an applicant (not an unrelated third party) and must meet the entitlement to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed common representative when none appointed
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple applicants do not appoint a common agent or common representative, the first-named applicant who has the right to file with the receiving Office will be considered the 'deemed common representative' of all applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deemed common representative may perform most acts on behalf of all applicants, including signing the request, demand and many other documents, but may not validly sign certain documents (e.g., notices effecting withdrawal, a designation, one or more priority claims, the demand or an election) on behalf of other applicants without evidence of their consent; if the deemed common representative has appointed an agent, that agent may perform similar acts but likewise cannot sign notices of withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for appointing an agent or common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: An appointment may be effected in the request and/or the demand, in a separate power of attorney, or in a general power of attorney; for multiple applicants a combination of methods may be used provided each applicant signs the request, the demand or a power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to specific paragraph references for required signatures and form; each applicant must sign one of the listed instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a separate power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appointment is effected by a separate power of attorney, that power must be submitted to either the receiving Office or the International Bureau, unless a waiver has been made by the Office/Authority/International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers are published in Official Notices, the PCT Newsletter and on WIPO website; waivers do not apply when the agent submits a notice of withdrawal (Rules 90bis.1–90bis.4). Model forms for a separate power of attorney are available on the WIPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for a general power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: A general power of attorney may appoint an agent to represent the applicant in relation to any international application filed by that applicant; the original general power of attorney must be filed with the receiving Office (or relevant Authority) and the appointment is effective for particular applications provided the general POA is referred to in the request, the demand or a separate notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices/Authorities may waive attaching a copy; where no waiver exists a copy must be attached but need not be separately signed. Waivers do not apply for withdrawal notices. Model forms available on WIPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effect of acts by an agent or common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act by or in relation to an agent or common representative has the effect of an act by or in relation to the applicant(s) whom the agent represents for the purposes of the PCT procedure before the receiving Office, IB, ISA, SISA and/or IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents can sign documents on behalf of applicants; the deemed common representative may not sign withdrawal notices on behalf of others; where multiple agents represent the same applicant(s), an act by any of them has effect as an act by the applicant(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of appointment of agent or common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment may be revoked; the revocation document must be signed by persons who made the appointment or their successors in title; appointment of a sub-agent is also considered revoked if the appointing agent's appointment is revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for signing and submission of a power of attorney apply mutatis mutandis to revocation (see paragraphs 11.007–11.009).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic effect of a new appointment on earlier appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment of an agent for the international phase in general automatically has the effect, unless otherwise indicated, of revoking any earlier such appointment; similarly for common representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A later appointment supersedes earlier ones unless otherwise specified in the appointment document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renunciation of appointment by agent/common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Renunciation may be made by means of a notification signed by the agent or common representative; the Rules for signing and submission of a power of attorney apply mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant is informed of the renunciation by the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing of correspondence in the international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a sole applicant correspondence will be sent to the applicant at the indicated address or, if agents have been appointed, to that agent (or first-mentioned); where multiple applicants with common agents correspondence will be sent to the common agent or first-mentioned; where no common agent to the common representative at the address indicated, or to that representative's appointed agent or special address if provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special addressing rules apply for agents appointed specifically before the ISA, SISA or IPEA (correspondence addressed to that specific agent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording changes to applicant, inventor, agent or common representative (Rule 92bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a change in the person, name, residence, nationality or address of the applicant, or in the person, name or address of the inventor, agent or common representative, the applicant or the receiving Office should ask the International Bureau to record the change, which the IB will do and notify Offices if so requested; recording is free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording should be requested to ensure all Offices and PCT Authorities are informed; see subsequent subcriteria for evidence, timing and method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended channel for sending requests for recording changes
rubrics_metrics.description: While Rule 92bis allows requests to be sent to the receiving Office or the International Bureau, it is strongly recommended to send them directly to the International Bureau, preferably via ePCT, so the IB receives the request in order to meet the applicable 30-month time limit from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using ePCT (with or without strong authentication) is recommended to ensure timely recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence required for recording changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally it is not necessary to produce documentary evidence when the applicant or agent requests a change to be recorded under Rule 92bis; assignments or other documentary evidence may be required by designated Offices in the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a person not named in the request (a new applicant) requests the change without written consent of the applicant of record, a copy of an assignment or other documentary evidence supporting the change must be filed; when the request is filed by a new agent for the new applicant, a power of attorney signed by the new applicant must be furnished unless waived by the Office/Authority (the IB has not waived this requirement when filing with the IB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of address when patent agent moves firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent agent changes to a new firm and requests that the change be recorded, such change will be treated as a change of address and a new power need not be furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a limited exception to the usual POA requirements for representation changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that new applicant need not be resident/national of a Contracting State
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary for a new applicant (for recording a change in person of the applicant) to be a resident or national of a PCT Contracting State; the PCT does not restrict to whom an international application may be assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant's right to file is determined solely by nationality/residence indicated at the time of filing; the residence/nationality of the new applicant matters for whether that applicant has the right to file a demand for international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other kinds of changes recordable under Rule 92bis
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes concerning addition or deletion of indications relating to applicants and/or inventors, order of applicants/inventors in the request form, changes relating to e-mail addresses etc. can be recorded under Rule 92bis if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not possible during the international phase to record rights of third parties (licenses, pledges, security interests); those must be recorded in the national phase per national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single request for changes affecting multiple international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a change concerns multiple pending international applications, applicants are recommended to submit a single written request including a list of the PCT applications concerned (only pending applications, i.e., within the 30-month limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This simplifies processing; do not include applications beyond the 30-month pending window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and language requirements for requests to record changes
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no special form for requests under Rule 92bis; a letter to the receiving Office or the International Bureau clearly specifying the application and which information is to be changed suffices; if the application uses non-Latin characters provide a transliteration or translation of new names/addresses into English in addition to the filing language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strongly recommended to file requests directly with the IB through ePCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to request recording of changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau records the change if it receives the request before expiration of 30 months from the priority date; if the request reaches the IB too late to be reflected in international publication but within 30 months it will still be acted upon; after 30 months the change will not be recorded and the applicant must proceed before each designated/elected Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30-month cutoff is mandatory for recording during the international phase; bibliographic data in PATENTSCOPE is updated until 30 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effect of changes recorded by the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, designated and elected Offices are obliged to accept changes recorded by the International Bureau, but Offices may require additional evidence or documents in the national phase regarding such changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Chapters list Offices requiring additional documents; the IB's recording facilitates national phase processing but does not override national evidence requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when applicant dies during the international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The successor to the rights of the applicant should be indicated as the new applicant and a request to record the change under Rule 92bis should be made; documentary evidence proving the right to the application is not required during the international phase (but may be required in national phase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate reason for change; designated Offices may later request proof during national processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating an inventor deceased before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inventor died before the international application was filed, the request must indicate the name of the deceased inventor with an indication that he/she is deceased (e.g., 'JONES, Bernard (deceased)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear textual indication should be used to show the inventor is deceased.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording death of inventor during the international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inventor died during the international phase, the recording of a change to indicate that the inventor is deceased may be requested; where such indication is added the inventor's address would be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 92bis change-recording process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing when an applicant is temporarily unavailable to sign
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant is temporarily unavailable the international application can be filed without that applicant's signature; the lack of signature or of a power of attorney are correctable defects under Article 14(1)(a)(i) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defects may be remedied by filing a signed copy (or POA) within the receiving Office's time limit for correction (see paragraph 6.032).

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule on rectification of obvious mistakes (Rule 91)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious mistakes in the international application or other documents submitted by the applicant may generally be rectified if the rectification is requested within the applicable time limit; rectification is effected free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 91 lists certain mistakes that are not rectifiable and alternative correction mechanisms (Rules 20.4, 20.5, 26bis, 38.3) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an 'obvious mistake' for rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: A mistake is 'obvious' if it is obvious to the competent authority that, at the relevant date, something else was intended than what appears in the document, and that nothing else could have been intended other than the proposed rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the mistake and the rectification must be obvious to the competent authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on documents considered for determining obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: If the mistake is in the description, claims or drawings (or a correction/amendment thereof), the competent authority is limited to take into account only the contents of the description, claims and drawings and any correction/amendment concerned; if the mistake is in the request or certain other documents, the authority should also consider any documents submitted by the applicant (including priority documents) and any documents in the authority's international application file at the relevant date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of what may be considered depends on the document in which the mistake appears; paragraph references specify the applicable document lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant date for determining obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the mistake appears in the international application as filed, the relevant date is the international filing date; where the mistake appears in any other document (including corrections or amendments), the relevant date is the date on which that document was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the filing date for mistakes in the application as filed, and the submission date for mistakes in later documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistakes that cannot be rectified under Rule 91
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes not rectifiable include: omissions of entire elements or sheets; mistakes in the abstract; mistakes in an Article 19 amendment (unless IPEA is competent); mistakes in a priority claim or notice correcting/adding priority if rectification would change the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must rely on other correction means (e.g., Rule 26bis) for such mistakes; examples include lost sheets or priority-date altering corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent authority for authorization of rectifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectifications must be authorized by the competent PCT authority: (i) mistakes in the request by the receiving Office; (ii) mistakes in description/claims/drawings or corrections thereof by the ISA (or by IPEA if demand made and certain conditions met); (iii) mistakes in those documents or Article 19/34 amendments by the IPEA in certain circumstances; (iv) mistakes in other documents by the Office/Authority/Bureau to which the document was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which authority is competent depends on the document containing the mistake and whether an international preliminary examination demand has been made and when the IPEA's competence arises (see Rule 91.1(b) and paragraph 11.038).

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and when to file a request for rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rectification must be addressed to the competent authority and filed within 26 months from the priority date; it must specify the mistake and the proposed rectification and may contain a brief explanation; Rule 26.4 applies as to how to indicate the proposed rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission within 26 months is required; include clear specification and proposed change using the prescribed manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may invite applicant to request rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving Office, ISA, IPEA or IB discovers what appears to be a rectifiable obvious mistake, it may invite the applicant to file a request for rectification under Rule 91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is discretionary and intended to assist applicants to correct obvious mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing steps and notifications after a rectification request
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a request for rectification is filed, the competent authority promptly decides to authorize or refuse and promptly notifies the applicant and the International Bureau; in case of refusal the authority should state reasons; where authorized, the document is rectified and publication/annexation procedures follow depending on which authority authorized the rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authorization is received by the IB before technical preparations for publication are complete the rectified sheets are published; otherwise the IB will republish later. If IPEA authorizes rectification, rectified sheets and the request are annexed to the IPRP (Chapter II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of an authorized rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the mistake appears in the international application as filed the rectification becomes effective as from the international filing date; if the mistake appears in any other document the rectification becomes effective from the date that document was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective date depends on where the mistake originated; this affects priority/entitlement considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's recourse and publication after refusal to authorize rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: If authorization is refused the applicant may request the International Bureau, within two months from the refusal date, to publish the request for rectification, the reasons for refusal and any brief comments by the applicant together with the international application, subject to payment of a special fee as indicated in Annex B (IB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once published the applicant may pursue rectification further before designated Offices under national law; refused requests are not annexed to the IPRP except in certain circumstances (see paragraph 10.076).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of authorized rectification on designated and elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated and elected Offices must generally process the international application in the national phase 'as rectified' unless that Office already started processing/examination before being notified of the authorization; otherwise an Office may disregard a rectification only if it finds that it would not have authorized the rectification itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an Office intends to disregard an authorized rectification it must give the applicant an opportunity to make observations within a reasonable time limit.
